Practised speed, velocity and acceleration using motion examples.
Calculated speed from distance ÷ time: 200 m ÷ 10 s = 20 m/s.
Calculated acceleration with a = (v − u)/t, including −5 m/s² and −2 m/s² cases.
Calculated average speed as total distance ÷ total time: 120 km ÷ 3 h = 40 km/h.
Teach-back was not passed; acceleration during slowing down remained unclear.
end.parentNote: A mix-up remained: they associated acceleration only with speeding up, and this was not corrected by the last example. At home, ask them to explain how a car can have acceleration when its velocity is decreasing, using a simple speed-time graph.
